+This set of contracts is related to the https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643[ERC-3643 T-REX Token Standard], an institutional grade security token standard.
+TIP: For an overview of ERC-3643 tokens and a walk through on how to create a token contract read our xref:ROOT:erc3643.adoc[ERC-3643 guide].
+* {ERC3643}: ERC-20 token that provides compliance-driven token transfers with identity verification, freezing capabilities, and regulatory controls.
+The interfaces defined by the standard are available in the xref:api:interfaces.adoc#IERC3643[Interfaces] section.

https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3643[ERC-3643] defines permissioned tokens: ERC-20 tokens that can only be held by verified investors and only move in ways the issuer's rules allow. It is the standard behind T-REX and is typically used to represent regulated assets such as securities or fund shares.

-OpenZeppelin Contracts provides the token, xref:api:token/ERC20.adoc#ERC3643[`ERC3643`], its interface, xref:api:interfaces.adoc#IERC3643[`IERC3643`], and the interfaces of the other components the standard defines, such as xref:api:interfaces.adoc#IERC3643IdentityRegistry[`IERC3643IdentityRegistry`] and xref:api:interfaces.adoc#IERC3643Compliance[`IERC3643Compliance`]. The identity registry and the compliance contract are left to the issuer's stack.

The hook is called by every function that needs authorization, so it discriminates between them through `msg.sig`. A token that must expose the ERC-173 `owner` and the xref:api:interfaces.adoc#IERC3643AgentRole[`IERC3643AgentRole`] functions adds them on top. As another example, xref:api:access.adoc#AccessManaged[`AccessManaged`] gives each function its own role. Batch functions reach the hook with their own selector.
